newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia power price hike not to boost inflation.
newsitem.headline: Russia power price hike not to boost inflation.

text.p: Plans by the Russian government to raise electricity prices for households are unlikely to push up inflation much, as electricity payments make up only a tiny part of the consumer basket, experts said on Friday.

"It will have only a very small impact on inflation," Irina Goryacheva, head of the price statistics department at the State Statistics Committee told Reuters. "Electricity expenses in the consumer basket makes some one-tenth of a percent."
The government plans to double electricity prices for households from October 1 to boost revenue to power generators and slash costs to industry.
Russian households currently pay from 37 to 200 roubles per kilowatt for electricity.
Russia's monthly inflation rate has fallen steadily this year to a post-reform low of 0.7 percent in July.
The State Statistics Committee has forecast that on current price trends prices will fall 0.2 percent over the whole of August, the first monthly fall since reforms began in 1992.
Yaroslav Lisovolik, an expert at the Russian-European Centre for Economic Policy, said the major inflationary factor was households' confidence in the rouble.

"The fundamental factor of public trust in the rouble, which is reflected in a fall in money velocity which can be seen over the last few months should compensate for the inflationary pressure of the rise in electricity prices," he said.
"It'll take an earthquake to raise inflation by two or three percent now," Goryacheva said. "It would take a mass price rise for most consumer goods, which is impossible."
